direction_as_read: mixed: modest pooled capsaicin effect on weight, null at the labels' amount in one acute trial, and small positive gut trials at other doses
summary: These labels sell whole cayenne (450-500 mg) or an extract (500 mg), and no label row shows a capsaicinoid amount. Two product names show heat units, which can't be read as a dose. Pooled capsaicin trials show a modest weight effect, about 0.5 kg (36938807); the abstract doesn't separate whole cayenne or extract. The one trial at the label form and amount, 500 mg cayenne with 1.25 mg capsaicin, was a single dose in 11 men and showed no thermogenic effect (24267043). Red pepper powder helped in small gut symptom trials, at 2.5 g/day (12030948) and in enteric-coated pills (21573941); neither is what these labels print. The evidence doesn't show benefit for the labels as printed.
